subject.title: refactor(infra): move exec approvals into the shared SQLite state DB

question: Should the file-to-SQLite cutover require upgraded users to run `openclaw doctor --fix` before every exec-approval-dependent runtime path, rather than preserve a temporary runtime compatibility reader?
rationale: The repository policy favors canonical runtime state with Doctor-owned migration, but this is still an intentional operator-facing fail-closed change on an execution authorization path and needs explicit maintainer acceptance backed by real upgrade evidence.

options.title: Accept the Doctor-gated cutover
options.body: Keep the proposed canonical SQLite-only runtime after redacted proof confirms legacy import, recovery messaging, and post-migration authorization behavior.

options.title: Add temporary runtime compatibility
options.body: Keep a legacy reader during an upgrade window, accepting additional state-path complexity and a longer removal plan.

options.title: Pause the migration
options.body: Keep the current file store and pursue only narrower lock-contention hardening until the upgrade transition is product-approved.

recommendation.title: Accept the Doctor-gated cutover
recommendation.body: Keep the proposed canonical SQLite-only runtime after redacted proof confirms legacy import, recovery messaging, and post-migration authorization behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The branch and the related merged mitigation show direct ownership of the exec-approvals persistence path.
